If the user wants something to happen automatically in response to an EVENT, they need a **hook** configured in settings.json. Memory/preferences cannot trigger automated actions.

- "Before compacting, ask me what to preserve" → PreCompact hook

**Always read the existing settings file before making changes.** Merge new settings with existing ones - never replace the entire file.

1	# INC-20 — Crash-orphaned undertaken work: no per-task commit/push, no four-state updates, while KStore hooks held the only record
2	
3	**Date**: 2026-11-01 (small hours; North-American DST fell back that night —
4	clock-time ordering is misleading, UTC is given)
5	**Project**: Natally (`~/Desktop/DevProjects/natally-ai-studio`), R12
6	landing-replica round
7	**Severity**: Workflow-discipline / publication gap — an OS-level crash
8	(GNOME restart) killed the orchestrator session mid-dispatch. Two coder
9	tasks' edits survived only as uncommitted working-tree changes; the round's
10	CHECKLIST four-state statuses were never updated; nothing was committed or
11	pushed. Recovery required the operator to hand-direct a three-way
12	reconciliation (git ↔ CHECKLIST ↔ KStore ↔ CodeGraph) that disciplined
13	execution would have made unnecessary.
14	
15	## Summary — observed timeline (UTC)
16	
17	- 05:40Z — operator exports the planning conversation to the repo root
18	  (`2026-11-01-014013-…-repair-landing-page.txt`).
19	- 06:00–06:01Z — R12 architecture and four-state coder tasklist written
20	  (`DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHECKLIST.md`; backups
21	  `*.bak.20261101_015555` beside originals).
22	- 06:03–06:04Z — round-state memory written; second conversation exported
23	  (`2026-11-01-010338-…-architected-and-checklist-ready-to-be-assigned-to-subagent-coders.txt`).
24	- Commits `e9522ff2` (architecture freeze), `df046b1b` (tasklist publish),
25	  `6c5b886c` (editorial cleanup) pushed to origin/master and
26	  remote-verified. Dispatch explicitly **HELD** for operator signoff.
27	- 06:15Z — `src/marketing.tsx` (R12-A scope) and
28	  `src/components/Astrolabe3D.tsx` (R12-B scope) edited by the next session:
29	  partial implementations of the frozen contracts.
30	- 06:19:45Z — KStore captures two parallel coder `session_meta` streams —
31	  dispatch had begun. CHECKLIST still read `assigned [ ]` and the round-level
32	  dispatch row still read NOT_STARTED/HOLD. No commit, no push, no marker
33	  flips.
34	- 08:10:34Z — last KStore hook event from that session (SessionEnd,
35	  session `d3fbc787-…`). Latest KStore review verdict remains 2026-10-28 —
36	  the crashed turns never reached a Stop review.
37	- ~08:12Z — GNOME restart; session context lost.
38	
39	## The reconciliation the operator had to direct
40	
41	| Authority | What it said | Agrees with |
42	|---|---|---|
43	| git (last commit `6c5b886c`) | Tasklist published; dispatch held; nothing assigned | CHECKLIST |
44	| CHECKLIST.md (committed = disk) | Same — all five tasks `assigned [ ]`, dispatch NOT_STARTED | git |
45	| Working tree / CodeGraph | Partial R12-A and partial R12-B already implemented, uncommitted; R12-C/D/E absent | KStore |
46	| KStore (hook captures) | Two coder sessions dispatched 06:19:45Z; activity continuing to 08:10:34Z | Working tree |
47	
48	Two consistent pairs, contradicting each other. The durable publication
49	surfaces (git + CHECKLIST) told one story; the passive capture fabric
50	(KStore) and the filesystem told the truth. Recovery was possible only
51	because (a) KStore hooks had captured everything as it happened, (b) the
52	operator had saved the two prior conversations to the repo root, and (c) the
53	R12 tasks were written idempotently, so the partial edits could be absorbed
54	by re-execution instead of being fatal.
55	
56	## Root cause
57	
58	Execution was undertaken without simultaneously maintaining the durable
59	state surfaces. Publication was treated as a task-completion-only event, so
60	all in-flight state — the dispatch itself, the assignment markers, the
61	partial edits — lived nowhere durable. The crash converted a discipline gap
62	into an incident: anything not committed, not checklisted, and not hooked
63	into KStore simply vanished; what remained had to be reconstructed by
64	forensics the operator had to supervise line by line.
65	
66	## Lesson — the three fastidious habits (canonical)
67	
68	1. **Commit and push every completed task immediately, and verify the
69	   remote.** A local commit or a deployed artifact is not publication. Never
70	   let a round's authorization, dispatch, or partial reviewed progress sit
71	   uncommitted — "the task isn't finished yet" is when the crash clock is
72	   running.
73	2. **Hooks send everything to KStore as you go — never bypass, never
74	   disable.** KStore was the only continuity channel that survived this
75	   crash intact. It is the single source of truth for "what was your last
76	   line": if you ask it, and your hooks are in order, it answers.
77	3. **Update the CHECKLIST four-state status fastidiously as you go.**
78	   Assignment `[/]`, undertaking, completion `[X]`, validation `✅` each
79	   flip at the moment they happen, so that at every instant git, CHECKLIST,
80	   and KStore agree. If you are compliant, all three match where you left
81	   off; if they do not match, the drift itself is the finding.
82	
83	## Why this binds globally
84	
85	Any session on any project can be killed by an OS crash, power loss, or
86	harness failure at any moment. The three habits are the only difference
87	between "resume from the durable record" and "archaeology under operator
88	supervision." They cost seconds per event; this incident cost a supervised
89	forensic reconstruction and risked silent loss of undertaken work.
90	
91	## Cross-references
92	
93	- Standing instruction in the project `CLAUDE.md` (commit and push every
94	  completed task; verify the remote; report publication gaps honestly).
95	- INC-3 (window-replacement orphan) — same crash-class, earlier substrate;
96	  INC-20 extends it from "orchestrator continuity" to "per-task publication
97	  + four-state + hook-capture discipline."
98	- INC-7 (proxy attestation / marker progression) — the four-state marker
99	  semantics this incident's checklist discipline depends on.
100	- `resumes-not-recovery-points` (git/KStore/task_ledger are the only
101	  authoritative recovery points; session resumes are not).

1	# INC-20 — Crash-orphaned undertaken work: no per-task commit/push, no four-state updates, while KStore hooks held the only record
2	
3	**Date**: 2026-11-01 (small hours; North-American DST fell back that night —
4	clock-time ordering is misleading, UTC is given)
5	**Project**: Natally (`~/Desktop/DevProjects/natally-ai-studio`), R12
6	landing-replica round
7	**Severity**: Workflow-discipline / publication gap — an OS-level crash
8	(GNOME restart) killed the orchestrator session mid-dispatch. Two coder
9	tasks' edits survived only as uncommitted working-tree changes; the round's
10	CHECKLIST four-state statuses were never updated; nothing was committed or
11	pushed. Recovery required the operator to hand-direct a three-way
12	reconciliation (git ↔ CHECKLIST ↔ KStore ↔ CodeGraph) that disciplined
13	execution would have made unnecessary.
14	
15	## Summary — observed timeline (UTC)
16	
17	- 05:40Z — operator exports the planning conversation to the repo root
18	  (`2026-11-01-014013-…-repair-landing-page.txt`).
19	- 06:00–06:01Z — R12 architecture and four-state coder tasklist written
20	  (`DOCS/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHECKLIST.md`; backups
21	  `*.bak.20261101_015555` beside originals).
22	- 06:03–06:04Z — round-state memory written; second conversation exported
23	  (`2026-11-01-010338-…-architected-and-checklist-ready-to-be-assigned-to-subagent-coders.txt`).
24	- Commits `e9522ff2` (architecture freeze), `df046b1b` (tasklist publish),
25	  `6c5b886c` (editorial cleanup) pushed to origin/master and
26	  remote-verified. Dispatch explicitly **HELD** for operator signoff.
27	- 06:15Z — `src/marketing.tsx` (R12-A scope) and
28	  `src/components/Astrolabe3D.tsx` (R12-B scope) edited by the next session:
29	  partial implementations of the frozen contracts.
30	- 06:19:45Z — KStore captures two parallel coder `session_meta` streams —
31	  dispatch had begun. CHECKLIST still read `assigned [ ]` and the round-level
32	  dispatch row still read NOT_STARTED/HOLD. No commit, no push, no marker
33	  flips.
34	- 08:10:34Z — last KStore hook event from that session (SessionEnd,
35	  session `d3fbc787-…`). Latest KStore review verdict remains 2026-10-28 —
36	  the crashed turns never reached a Stop review.
37	- ~08:12Z — GNOME restart; session context lost.
38	
39	## The reconciliation the operator had to direct
40	
41	| Authority | What it said | Agrees with |
42	|---|---|---|
43	| git (last commit `6c5b886c`) | Tasklist published; dispatch held; nothing assigned | CHECKLIST |
44	| CHECKLIST.md (committed = disk) | Same — all five tasks `assigned [ ]`, dispatch NOT_STARTED | git |
45	| Working tree / CodeGraph | Partial R12-A and partial R12-B already implemented, uncommitted; R12-C/D/E absent | KStore |
46	| KStore (hook captures) | Two coder sessions dispatched 06:19:45Z; activity continuing to 08:10:34Z | Working tree |
47	
48	Two consistent pairs, contradicting each other. The durable publication
49	surfaces (git + CHECKLIST) told one story; the passive capture fabric
50	(KStore) and the filesystem told the truth. Recovery was possible only
51	because (a) KStore hooks had captured everything as it happened, (b) the
52	operator had saved the two prior conversations to the repo root, and (c) the
53	R12 tasks were written idempotently, so the partial edits could be absorbed
54	by re-execution instead of being fatal.
55	
56	## Root cause
57	
58	Execution was undertaken without simultaneously maintaining the durable
59	state surfaces. Publication was treated as a task-completion-only event, so
60	all in-flight state — the dispatch itself, the assignment markers, the
61	partial edits — lived nowhere durable. The crash converted a discipline gap
62	into an incident: anything not committed, not checklisted, and not hooked
63	into KStore simply vanished; what remained had to be reconstructed by
64	forensics the operator had to supervise line by line.
65	
66	## Lesson — the three fastidious habits (canonical)
67	
68	1. **Commit and push every completed task immediately, and verify the
69	   remote.** A local commit or a deployed artifact is not publication. Never
70	   let a round's authorization, dispatch, or partial reviewed progress sit
71	   uncommitted — "the task isn't finished yet" is when the crash clock is
72	   running.
73	2. **Hooks send everything to KStore as you go — never bypass, never
74	   disable.** KStore was the only continuity channel that survived this
75	   crash intact. It is the single source of truth for "what was your last
76	   line": if you ask it, and your hooks are in order, it answers.
77	3. **Update the CHECKLIST four-state status fastidiously as you go.**
78	   Assignment `[/]`, undertaking, completion `[X]`, validation `✅` each
79	   flip at the moment they happen, so that at every instant git, CHECKLIST,
80	   and KStore agree. If you are compliant, all three match where you left
81	   off; if they do not match, the drift itself is the finding.
82	
83	## Why this binds globally
84	
85	Any session on any project can be killed by an OS crash, power loss, or
86	harness failure at any moment. The three habits are the only difference
87	between "resume from the durable record" and "archaeology under operator
88	supervision." They cost seconds per event; this incident cost a supervised
89	forensic reconstruction and risked silent loss of undertaken work.
90	
91	## Cross-references
92	
93	- Standing instruction in the project `CLAUDE.md` (commit and push every
94	  completed task; verify the remote; report publication gaps honestly).
95	- INC-3 (window-replacement orphan) — same crash-class, earlier substrate;
96	  INC-20 extends it from "orchestrator continuity" to "per-task publication
97	  + four-state + hook-capture discipline."
98	- INC-7 (proxy attestation / marker progression) — the four-state marker
99	  semantics this incident's checklist discipline depends on.
100	- `resumes-not-recovery-points` (git/KStore/task_ledger are the only
101	  authoritative recovery points; session resumes are not).

1	# TC10 — Commit and Push Every Task Completion and Handback
2	
3	**Severity: HIGH — prevent lost work and divergent histories across concurrently
4	active agents and machines. Binding for every agent role and runtime.**
5	
6	## 0. The rule
7	
8	At each completed task and handback, review the task's artifacts, stage only its
9	changes, commit, immediately push through the configured HTTPS Forgejo origin,
10	and verify the push and remote commit reachability. A local-only commit is an
11	incomplete delivery. Unrelated dirty work is preserved; it does not excuse leaving
12	a completed task unpushed. Do not require repeated approval for this standing
13	instruction.
14	
15	In a shared checkout, name one integrator to publish each worker's completed
16	handback promptly. Workers report exact files, verification, and gaps without
17	racing shared Git mutations. This coordinates the delivery obligation; it does
18	not defer it until the end of a multi-task project. Direct single-agent sessions
19	perform their own commit and push.
20	
21	## 1. Why push has priority
22	
23	The operator runs concurrent agents on multiple machines. A local commit protects
24	against some working-tree losses but remains invisible to the next machine; that
25	machine can continue from another ancestor and create divergent histories. Push
26	is part of task completion because prompt shared visibility prevents that failure.
27	Uncommitted changes also risk loss through cleanup, mistaken reset, or interrupted
28	handoff. A filesystem edit is durable on disk until changed or lost; compaction
29	alone does not delete it, but can lose the context needed to identify and recover
30	it. Commit plus verified publication preserves both content and provenance.
31	
32	Apply SC3's “net of all” ranked multicriteria judgment. Short means this handback;
33	medium means the next task and concurrent sessions; long means recovery and future
34	maintenance. Assess every available fact, including inconsistent lineage, unknown
35	remote state, large historical blobs, and the cost of publication.
36	
37	| Priority | Criterion and rationale | Option | Short horizon | Medium horizon | Long horizon |
38	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
39	| 1 | Preserve all work and repository integrity; losing another agent's changes defeats delivery | Scoped commit, integrate, verify push | Review and integration effort | Shared reachable work; preserved concurrent edits | Auditable recoverable history |
40	| 1 | Same criterion | Commit locally and stop, or overwrite remote | Less immediate effort | Divergent histories or lost changes | Recovery burden and possible repository breakage |
41	| 2 | Complete authorized work without operator dependency | Publish through verified HTTPS origin | Pays bounded push cost; reports actual failures | Next machine can continue | Repeatable autonomous delivery |
42	| 2 | Same criterion | Defer publication or seek repeated permission | Incomplete handback | Operator must reconcile hidden work | Recurring workflow dependency |
43	| 3 | Minimize total effort after integrity and completion | Integrate scoped work now | Small review/push cost | Avoids accumulating divergence | Lower cumulative recovery cost |
44	| 3 | Same criterion | Optimize only immediate time | Fast local finish | Later reconciliation cost grows | Hidden fragility persists |
45	
46	Selected: scoped commit AND verified push at every completion and handback.
47	A transient transport failure is an observed uncertainty, not permission to claim
48	success. A remote endpoint's primacy does not make its conflicting contents win
49	automatically; use SC3's complete-evidence matrix to reconcile them.
50	
51	## 2. Executable delivery procedure
52	
53	1. Inspect the current branch, worktree changes, configured fetch/push URLs, and
54	   local/remote Git graph. Fetch before deciding how to integrate. For Admin-Manual,
55	   the primary origin is `https://forgejo.robin.mba/rcheung/Admin-Manual.git`
56	   (Forgejo v15); obsolete `git.robin.mba` SSH guidance does not apply.
57	2. Review the completed task and its observed acceptance. Stage explicit paths,
58	   or selected hunks when files also contain another task's work. Do not use
59	   `git add -A` or `git add .` to sweep unrelated changes into the commit. Include
60	   the task's checklist update with truthful implementation/verification markers.
61	3. Commit with a semantic message naming the task. Preserve unrelated changes in
62	   place; use an isolated publishing worktree if the current checkout cannot
63	   safely express the scoped change. Keep snapshots, patches, and handoff files
64	   under `~/Admin-Manual/.staging/` or another semantic repository-owned path.
65	4. Integrate incoming work additively and inspect conflicts. Never force-push or
66	   discard another agent's commits. If historical cleanup has made lineages
67	   incompatible, use a clean authoritative publishing lineage and apply only the
68	   task's reviewed changes or scoped cherry-picks. Inspect reachability so this
69	   does not reintroduce pruned large blobs or unrelated local policy/history.
70	5. Push immediately to the configured HTTPS primary. Honor established branch
71	   protection: use an authorized task branch/PR path where required. An isolated
72	   `codex/` work branch is a reversible implementation choice when necessary to
73	   preserve concurrent work; do not invent an approval gate for it.
74	6. Check the push exit status, fetch the destination branch, and verify that the
75	   published task commit is an ancestor of its remote-tracking ref. Exact tip
76	   equality is unnecessary if another agent has already advanced the branch.
77	   For a scoped cherry-pick, record the source-to-published commit mapping and
78	   compare the intended changes. `git ls-remote` confirms the remote branch tip;
79	   `git merge-base --is-ancestor <published-sha> <fetched-remote-ref>` verifies
80	   continued reachability.
81	7. Report the task commit, destination branch, push result, and observed
82	   verification. If GitHub is configured as a mirror, publish only from a lineage
83	   compatible with its history and file limits; report an actual mirror rejection
84	   independently of primary delivery. Do not fabricate an outage or rewrite
85	   history to conceal a large-file rejection.
86	
87	If a push is rejected because another agent advanced the branch, fetch, integrate
88	without rewriting shared history, and retry. If the transport actually fails,
89	investigate the observed error and retry a bounded number of times when useful;
90	keep the commit and scoped recovery artifact, report the exact durability gap,
91	and continue independent authorized work. Never describe a failed or unattempted
92	push as successful, or silently defer publication because unrelated WIP exists.
93	
94	## 3. Relationship to workflow rules
95	
96	I-10(c) per-item delivery, I-17 delegated paperwork, and I-18 handback discipline
97	all use this procedure. I-8 governs durable staging; I-7 keeps CHECKLIST acceptance
98	as repeatable end-state assertions. Publication is an operational delivery action,
99	not a side-effecting CHECKLIST acceptance test. Commit reachability is an allowed
100	end-state assertion; a live remote poll is delivery evidence rather than a stable
101	CHECKLIST gate.
102	
103	Canonical policy: `global-agent-rules.md`. Runtime `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`
104	are equivalent routers to Admin-Manual, not separate stores for copied TC10 text.
105	This convention governs agents, not the human operator's personal Git cadence.
106

1	Refresh and follow all conventions in `/home/robin/Admin-Manual`, the global single source of truth.
2	
3	ALWAYS COMPLY WITH ~/Admin-Manual/ and nothing else.
4

18	not defer it until the end of a multi-task project. Direct single-agent sessions
19	perform their own commit and push.

21	## 1. Why push has priority
22	
23	The operator runs concurrent agents on multiple machines. A local commit protects
24	against some working-tree losses but remains invisible to the next machine; that
25	machine can continue from another ancestor and create divergent histories. Push
26	is part of task completion because prompt shared visibility prevents that failure.
27	Uncommitted changes also risk loss through cleanup, mistaken reset, or interrupted
28	handoff. A filesystem edit is durable on disk until changed or lost; compaction
29	alone does not delete it, but can lose the context needed to identify and recover
30	it. Commit plus verified publication preserves both content and provenance.
31	
32	Apply SC3's “net of all” ranked multicriteria judgment. Short means this handback;
33	medium means the next task and concurrent sessions; long means recovery and future
34	maintenance. Assess every available fact, including inconsistent lineage, unknown
35	remote state, large historical blobs, and the cost of publication.

46	Selected: scoped commit AND verified push at every completion and handback.

52	
53	1. Inspect the current branch, worktree changes, configured fetch/push URLs, and

65	4. Integrate incoming work additively and inspect conflicts. Never force-push or
66	   discard another agent's commits. If historical cleanup has made lineages
67	   incompatible, use a clean authoritative publishing lineage and apply only the
68	   task's reviewed changes or scoped cherry-picks. Inspect reachability so this
69	   does not reintroduce pruned large blobs or unrelated local policy/history.

76	   equality is unnecessary if another agent has already advanced the branch.

# TC19 — Three Authorities Agree at Every Instant (INC-20 mechanical enforcement)

**Severity: HIGH — the difference between "resume from the durable record" and
"archaeology under operator supervision" after any crash. Binding for every
agent role in every CHECKLIST.md-bearing repo: orchestrator, dispatched
coder, verifier.**

## 0. The invariant

At every instant, the three durable authorities must tell the same story
about where work left off:

| Authority | Surface | Records |
|---|---|---|
| **git** | last commit (+ verified remote reachability) | what has been published |
| **CHECKLIST** | four-state markers in the round's `CHECKLIST.md` | what is assigned / undertaken / completed / validated |
| **KStore** | hook captures (`session_meta`, tool events, `SessionEnd`) | what actually happened, as it happened |

If you are compliant, all three match where you left off. If they do not
match, **the drift itself is the finding** — report it, never paper over it.

The invariant is maintained by the three fastidious habits (canonical in
[INC-20](../INCIDENTS/crash-orphaned-undertaken-work-no-per-task-commit-no-four-state.md)):

1. **Commit and push every completed task immediately, and verify the
   remote.** A local commit or a deployed artifact is not publication. Round
   authorization, dispatch, and partial reviewed progress never sit
   uncommitted — "the task isn't finished yet" is when the crash clock runs.
2. **Hooks send everything to KStore as you go — never bypass, never
   disable.** KStore is the single source of truth for "what was your last
   line"; in INC-20 it was the only continuity channel that survived the
   crash intact.
3. **Flip the CHECKLIST four-state markers as-you-go, never in batch
   afterwards.** `[ ]` → `[/]` (assigned) → `[X]` (coder completes; capital
   X mandatory) → `✅` (verifier semantically attests) — marker semantics
   per INC-7. Each marker flips at the moment it happens.

## 1. Why prose enforcement failed

INC-20 (Natally R12, 2026-11-01): a GNOME restart killed the dispatch
session with two coders' edits uncommitted, CHECKLIST untouched, nothing
pushed. The standing rule "commit and push every completed task" already
existed — in project `CLAUDE.md`, in TC10, in the round's own instructions.
The crashed session read it and undertook work anyway, deferring publication
to "when the tasks complete." Prose states a deadline the harness cannot
see; nothing mechanical fires when it is missed. The operator's correction
(2026-11-01): *this incident requires improving the global-rules enforcement
that would have produced more fastidious compliance — not just writing the
incident up.* Enforcement therefore moved from prose to harness-executed
hooks: a reminder that is present at every prompt, and a gate that fires at
the only deadline the harness can observe — **when the turn tries to end**.

## 2. The enforcement (mechanisms, not exhortation)

Both scripts live in `~/.claude/hooks/` and are active only when the working
directory's repo root contains a `CHECKLIST.md` (round-driven projects);
other repos are unaffected.

### 2.1 `inject-inc20-discipline.sh` — UserPromptSubmit injector

Wired into `hooks.UserPromptSubmit` in `~/.claude/settings.json` (beside
`inject-rules.py` / `inject-violations.py` / `inject-phase-reminders.py`).
Emits `additionalContext` carrying the one-line standing discipline — the
three habits plus the invariant — so it is in context at every prompt of
every session in a CHECKLIST repo, not only in CLAUDE.md prose the session
may have read once.

### 2.2 `inc20-publication-gate.sh` — Stop publication gate (blocking)

Wired into `hooks.Stop` (beside `post-turn-review.py` /
`detect-violations-post-turn.py` and the KStore adapter). When the turn ends
in a CHECKLIST repo it checks:

- **Uncommitted working-tree changes** — untracked lines filtered to exclude
  only: `*.bak*` snapshots, dated conversation exports
  (`YYYY-MM-DD-*.txt`), and `.codegraph/`. The exclusion list is explicit
  and closed; nothing else is ignored by blanket rule.
- **Unpushed commits** — `git log @{u}..HEAD`.

If either is non-empty the hook **exits 2 (blocking)** with the offending
files/commits listed and the remedy stated: publish now (commit+push each
completed task per TC10, verify the remote, flip four-state markers as you
go). The turn cannot end silently over unpublished work.

### 2.3 Conscious override (never silent)

Legitimately in-flight work (a task mid-implementation at turn end) is not a
violation. The escape hatch is deliberate, per-session, and reported:

```
touch /tmp/inc20-stop-override-<session_id>
```

…then **state the reason in the final message**. The override lives in
`/tmp` keyed by session id (vanishes with the machine session, cannot
accumulate), and using it without declaring it is itself a violation of
TC18's deviations-reporting duty.

### 2.4 KStore capture (habit 2 — keep it wired)

The `kstore_claude_adapter` is wired in `~/.claude/settings.json` on
`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `SessionStart`,
`SessionEnd`, `UserPromptSubmit` and `Stop`. TC19 adds no new capture — it
forbids unwiring it: any session found running with KStore hooks bypassed or
disabled is non-compliant, whatever its reason (see
`claude-kstore-only.md`, `kstore-runtime-deployment-and-notification.md`).

## 3. Wiring and rebuild

- Canonical hook scripts: `~/.claude/hooks/inject-inc20-discipline.sh`,
  `~/.claude/hooks/inc20-publication-gate.sh` (created 2026-11-01; the
  orchestrator session that authored them wired them into
  `~/.claude/settings.json` the same night — verify with
  `grep -l inc20 ~/.claude/settings.json` when rebuilding).
- `scripts/kickstart-agent-runtime.sh` restores the `~/.claude/` runtime
  regime on a fresh workstation; TC19's scripts and their settings entries
  belong in that restore set. Runtime `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` files are
  routers to this document, not separate stores for copied TC19 text (same
  policy as TC10 §3).
- Repo applicability trigger: presence of `CHECKLIST.md` at the git root.

## 4. Relationship to other rules

- **TC10** (commit and push every task completion and handback) is the
  *delivery procedure* — how to stage, commit, push, verify reachability.
  TC19 is the *invariant and the gate* — when you may stop. INC-20 hardened
  TC10 with "verify the remote" and precipitated TC19.
- **INC-7** defines the four-state marker semantics TC19's flips depend on;
  **INC-3** is the same crash-class on an earlier substrate;
  `resumes-not-recovery-points` (auto-memory) fixes git/KStore/task_ledger
  as the only authoritative recovery points.
- **TC18**: an exercised override is a deviation to report; a blocked Stop
  that was overridden without declaration is an unattributed failure.

## 5. Status

Adopted 2026-11-01 from INC-20. Scripts in place; gate is blocking for all
CHECKLIST.md-bearing repos. First live round under the gate: Natally R12
dispatch (workflow `wf_83d8b679-fc2`). Amend this file when the exclusion
list or override protocol changes — never edit the scripts away from this
document.
